unit: Ch 7: Tax Deduction or Collection at Source and Advance Tax
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Basics of Deduction/Collection at Source & Direct Payment
explain: Income tax is recovered during the tax year through TDS, TCS, advance tax, or employer tax on non-monetary perquisites.
Tax deducted or collected at source is treated as tax paid on behalf of the person earning the income.
If no TDS provision applies or tax was not deducted, the assessee must pay tax directly under Section 391.
Failure by the deductor or assessee to pay tax makes the defaulting deductor an assessee-in-default.

flow.title: How tax collection at source works
steps: Deduct or collect tax at source

topics.example: An employer deducts tax from an employee's monthly salary and pays it to the Government as tax paid on behalf of the employee.
remember: TDS/TCS is payment of tax on behalf of the deductee.
Direct payment under Section 391 applies when tax is not deducted at source.
mistakes: Assuming direct payment by deductee automatically relieves the deductor from being treated as an assessee-in-default if TDS was missed.

quiz.q: Under Section 391, when is tax payable directly by the assessee?
o: When there is no TDS provision or tax was not deducted
Only if advance tax was paid
quiz.why: Section 391 requires direct payment if there is no TDS provision or if tax was not deducted as required.

quiz.q: Tax deducted at source is treated as payment of tax on behalf of whom?
o: The person from whose income tax was deducted
quiz.why: Section 390(3) specifies that TDS/TCS is treated as tax paid on behalf of the person earning the income.

topics.title: TDS on Salary & Accumulation in Provident Fund
explain: Employers must deduct TDS on salary at average rates at the time of payment based on estimated total income.
Default tax regime under Section 202(1) applies unless the employee intimates opting out under Section 202(4).
Employers can opt to pay tax on non-monetary perquisites at the average rate of tax.
Premature taxable withdrawal from RPF attracts 10% TDS under Section 392(7) if aggregate payment is ₹50,000 or more.

flow.title: Steps for deducting salary TDS
steps: Estimate employee total income for year
Apply tax rates under chosen regime
Calculate average rate of income tax
Deduct TDS at time of payment

topics.example: An employee withdrawing ₹60,000 prematurely from RPF before completing 5 years of service faces 10% TDS on the payout.
remember: Salary TDS arises ONLY at the time of payment, not accrual.
RPF premature withdrawal threshold is ₹50,00, deducted @10%.
mistakes: Deducting TDS on salary at the time of accrual instead of actual payment.

quiz.q: At what point is tax deductible at source from salary under Section 392?
o: At the end of financial year
quiz.why: Section 392(1) explicitly states that TDS on salary arises only at the time of payment.

quiz.q: What is the rate of TDS under Section 392(7) on premature taxable RPF withdrawal of ₹50,000 or more?
quiz.why: Section 392(7) prescribes 10% TDS on taxable premature RPF withdrawals.

topics.title: TDS on Insurance Commission, General Commission & Rent
explain: Insurance commission exceeding ₹20,000 attracts TDS at 2% for non-domestic companies and 10% for domestic companies.
Commission or brokerage paid by specified persons exceeding ₹20,000 attracts 2% TDS.
Rent paid by individuals/HUFs (not specified persons) exceeding ₹50,000/month attracts 2% TDS under Sl. No. 2(i).
Rent paid by specified persons attracts 2% on plant/machinery and 10% on land/building/furniture if monthly rent exceeds ₹50,000.
topics.example: A company paying monthly rent of ₹60,000 for an office building deducts TDS at 10% under Section 393(1).
remember: Rent by non-specified Individual/HUF: 2% TDS if monthly rent exceeds ₹50,000.
Specified person threshold: Business turnover > ₹1 crore, Profession > ₹50 lakhs in preceding year.
mistakes: Thinking individuals deducting rent TDS under Sl. No. 2(i) need to obtain a TAN. No TAN is required!

quiz.q: What is the TDS rate under Section 393(1) for rent paid on plant and machinery by a specified person?
quiz.why: Rent for plant, machinery, or equipment attracts 2% TDS when paid by a specified person.

quiz.q: An individual not subject to tax audit pays monthly house rent of ₹55,000. What is the TDS rate?
quiz.why: Rent paid by non-specified individuals exceeding ₹50,000 per month attracts 2% TDS under Sl. No. 2(i).

topics.title: TDS on Transfer of Immovable Property & Compulsory Acquisition
explain: Buying immovable property (except rural agricultural land) for consideration or stamp duty value of ₹50 lakhs or more attracts 1% TDS.
TDS is calculated at 1% on consideration or stamp duty value, whichever is higher.
Buyers deducting tax on property transfers are exempt from obtaining TAN.
Compulsory acquisition of urban immovable property exceeding ₹5,00,000 compensation attracts 10% TDS.

flow.title: Property transfer TDS test
steps: Compare consideration and Stamp Duty Value
Take higher of the two values
Check if value is ₹50 lakhs or more

topics.example: A buyer purchases a house for ₹60 lakhs with a stamp duty value of ₹85 lakhs; 1% TDS of ₹85,000 is deducted on ₹85 lakhs.
remember: Property TDS threshold: ₹50,00,000 (consideration or SDV).
Rate: 1% on higher of consideration or SDV.
mistakes: Calculating 1% TDS on consideration alone when stamp duty value is higher.

quiz.q: What is the threshold limit for TDS on transfer of immovable property under Section 393(1)?
quiz.why: TDS applies if consideration or stamp duty value of immovable property is ₹50,00,000 or more.

quiz.q: If house purchase consideration is ₹60 lakhs and SDV is ₹70 lakhs, TDS is 1% of which amount?
quiz.why: TDS is calculated on consideration or stamp duty value, whichever is higher.

topics.title: TDS on Mutual Fund Units & Interest Income
explain: Income in respect of mutual fund units exceeding ₹10,000 in a tax year attracts 10% TDS.
Interest on securities exceeding ₹10,000 attracts 10% TDS, with specific exemptions like 54EC capital gain bonds.
Interest other than securities paid by banks/co-operatives/post office attracts 10% TDS above ₹50,000 (₹1,00,000 for senior citizens).
Interest paid by other specified persons attracts 10% TDS if aggregate interest exceeds ₹10,000.
topics.example: A bank pays ₹65,000 FD interest to a senior citizen; no TDS is deducted as it is below the ₹1,00,000 threshold.
remember: Bank FD interest threshold: ₹1,00,000 for senior citizens, ₹50,000 for others.
TDS rate on interest is 10%.
mistakes: Applying the ₹10,000 threshold for bank interest when payee is a senior citizen.

quiz.q: What is the threshold for TDS on bank FD interest paid to a senior citizen under Section 393(1)?
quiz.why: The threshold for senior citizens on bank/co-operative/post office interest is ₹1,00,000.

quiz.q: What is the rate of TDS on interest on securities under Section 393(1)?
quiz.why: Interest on securities attracts TDS at 10% when exceeding ₹10,000.

topics.title: TDS on Contractors & Professional or Technical Fees
explain: Payment to contractors attracts 1% TDS (Individual/HUF) or 2% (others) if single sum exceeds ₹30,000 or aggregate exceeds ₹1,00,000.
Transport contractors owning 10 or less goods carriages with PAN declaration are exempt from TDS.
Payments by non-specified Individuals/HUFs for contract, professional, or commission work exceeding ₹50,00,000 attract 2% TDS.

Fees for technical services (FTS), call centre operation, and film royalty attract 2% TDS; professional fees, other royalty, non-compete fees, and director fees attract 10% TDS (threshold ₹50,000 each, except director fees which has no threshold).
topics.example: A firm pays ₹60,000 professional fees and ₹40,000 technical fees to an expert; TDS applies at 10% only on ₹60,000 professional fees.
remember: Contractor TDS: 1% (Individual/HUF), 2% (Others).
FTS/Technical fees: 2%; Professional fees: 10% (Threshold ₹50,000 each).
Director fees: 10% TDS with NO threshold limit.
mistakes: Aggregating professional fees and technical fees together to apply the ₹50,000 threshold.

quiz.q: What is the TDS rate on fees for technical services (not being professional services) under Section 393(1)?
quiz.why: Fees for technical services attract TDS at 2% under Sl. No. 6(iii).

quiz.q: What is the threshold limit for TDS on director sitting fees/remuneration under Section 393(1)?
quiz.why: Director remuneration/fees not covered under salary has no threshold limit and attracts 10% TDS on any amount.

topics.title: TDS on Dividends, LIC Payments & Purchase of Goods
explain: Dividend declared by domestic company attracts 10% TDS if distributed to an individual by non-cash mode exceeding ₹10,000.
Payment under LIC policy (not exempt under Schedule II) exceeding ₹1,00,000 attracts 2% TDS on the income component.
Buyer purchasing goods exceeding ₹50 lakhs in a tax year (with preceding year business turnover > ₹10 crores) deducts 0.1% TDS on sum exceeding ₹50 lakhs.
Specified senior citizens (75+ years with only pension & same bank interest) have tax deducted by specified banks with return filing exemption.
Business benefits or perquisites exceeding ₹20,000 attract 10% TDS under Sl. No. 8(iv).

flow.title: TDS on purchase of goods process

topics.example: A buyer with ₹12 crore turnover purchases goods for ₹72 lakhs from a seller; TDS is 0.1% on ₹22 lakhs (₹72L - ₹50L) = ₹2,200.
remember: Goods purchase TDS: 0.1% on amount exceeding ₹50 lakhs.
Buyer eligibility: Preceding year turnover > ₹10 crores.
LIC payout TDS: 2% on income portion if payout > ₹1,00,000.
mistakes: Deducting 0.1% TDS on the entire purchase value instead of only the amount exceeding ₹50 lakhs.

quiz.q: Under Section 393(1) Sl. No. 8(ii), what is the rate of TDS on purchase of goods exceeding ₹50 lakhs?
quiz.why: TDS on purchase of goods exceeding ₹50 lakhs is 0.1% on the excess amount.

quiz.q: What preceding year turnover must a buyer have to be liable for TDS on purchase of goods?
quiz.why: A buyer is defined as a person whose turnover from business exceeded ₹10 crores in the preceding tax year.

topics.title: TDS on Winnings, Online Games & Sums Paid to Partners
explain: Winnings from lottery, crossword puzzles, card games, gambling, or horse races exceeding ₹10,000 in a single transaction attract 30% TDS.
Winnings from online games attract 30% TDS on net winnings at the end of the tax year or at the time of withdrawal.
Commission on sale of lottery tickets exceeding ₹20,000 attracts 2% TDS.
Cash withdrawals from banks/co-operatives/post office exceeding ₹1 crore (₹3 crores for co-op societies) attract 2% TDS.
Partnership firms paying salary, remuneration, bonus, or interest to partners exceeding ₹20,000 in aggregate attract 10% TDS.

flow.title: Handling TDS on online game winnings
steps: Track net winnings in user account
Check for user withdrawals during year
Deduct 30% TDS on net winnings at year-end

topics.example: A partnership firm pays ₹30,000 interest to a partner; 10% TDS (₹3,000) is deducted under Section 393(3) Sl. No. 7.
remember: Lottery / Horse Race / Online Games TDS rate: 30%.
Cash withdrawal TDS: 2% on cash exceeding ₹1 crore.
Partner payment TDS: 10% if exceeding ₹20,000.
mistakes: Applying a threshold limit of ₹10,000 for online game winnings. Online games have no minimum threshold!

quiz.q: What is the rate of TDS on winnings from online games under Section 393(3)?
quiz.why: Winnings from online games attract TDS at 30% on net winnings.

quiz.q: What is the threshold for TDS on salary/interest paid by a firm to its partner?
quiz.why: Firm payments to partners attract 10% TDS if the aggregate amount exceeds ₹20,000.

topics.title: Lower or Nil Deduction Declarations & Net of TDS Rules
explain: No TDS applies on payments to Government, RBI, tax-exempt statutory corporations, or Mutual Funds under Section 393(5).

Resident individuals can furnish a written declaration for Nil TDS under Section 393(6) if total tax on estimated total income is Nil and income is within basic exemption limit (exemption limit condition doesn't apply to senior citizens).
Payees can apply to the Assessing Officer for a lower/nil deduction certificate under Section 395(1).
If a contract states tax is borne by the payer, income is grossed up under Section 393(10) so net amount paid equals agreed sum after tax deduction.

flow.title: Grossing up income when tax is borne by payer
steps: Deduct tax on grossed up income

topics.example: A resident senior citizen with total tax liability of Nil submits a declaration to the bank for zero TDS on FD interest.
remember: Non-senior citizens can file Nil TDS declaration ONLY if income is within basic exemption limit.
Grossing up applies when tax is borne by the payer.
mistakes: Assuming a non-senior citizen can file a Nil TDS declaration when their total income exceeds the basic exemption limit.

quiz.q: Can a non-senior citizen furnish a declaration for Nil TDS under Section 393(6) if their income exceeds the basic exemption limit?
o: Yes, if tax payable is Nil
quiz.why: Section 393(6) prohibits non-senior citizens from submitting a Nil TDS declaration if aggregate income exceeds the basic exemption limit.

quiz.q: When tax on an income is to be borne by the payer, how is TDS computed under Section 393(10)?
o: Tax is deducted on net amount
Income is grossed up before applying TDS rate
Tax is collected from recipient later
quiz.why: Section 393(10) requires income to be increased (grossed up) to an amount that leaves the net payable amount after deducting tax.

topics.title: Tax Collection at Source (TCS) Provisions
explain: Sellers collect TCS on specified goods: alcoholic liquor (2%), tendu leaves (2%), timber/forest produce (2%), scrap (2%), minerals (2%).
Licensor/lessor collects 2% TCS on use of parking lot, toll plaza, or mine/quarry for business.
Motor vehicle or notified goods sale consideration exceeding ₹10 lakhs attracts 1% TCS at retail level per vehicle.
LRS overseas remittances exceeding ₹10 lakhs attract 2% TCS (education/medical) or 20% TCS (other purposes).
Sale of overseas tour packages attracts 2% TCS with no threshold limit.

flow.title: TCS collection workflow
steps: Collect TCS at debit or receipt

topics.example: An authorized dealer remits ₹12 lakhs under LRS for investment; TCS is collected at 20% on ₹2 lakhs (amount exceeding ₹10 lakhs).
remember: Motor car TCS: 1% if sale price exceeds ₹10 lakhs per vehicle.
LRS threshold: Combined ₹10 lakhs per remitter per year.
Overseas tour package TCS: 2% (No threshold).
mistakes: Applying the ₹10 lakh LRS threshold separately for education, medical, and other purposes instead of a combined threshold.

quiz.q: What is the TCS rate on sale of an overseas tour programme package under Section 394?
quiz.why: Sale of overseas tour packages attracts 2% TCS under Section 394(1) Sl. No. 8.

quiz.q: What is the TCS rate for LRS remittance exceeding ₹10 lakhs for purposes other than education or medical treatment?
quiz.why: LRS remittances for other purposes exceeding ₹10 lakhs attract TCS at 20%.

topics.title: TAN, PAN Consequences & Deposit or Filing Rules
explain: Every deductor/collector must obtain and quote TAN in all challans, statements, and certificates (exempt for individual rent/property TDS).
Deductee/collectee must furnish valid PAN; non-furnishing attracts higher TDS rate (higher of prescribed rate, rate in force, or 20%/5% for goods purchase) and higher TCS (twice rate or 5%, max 20%).
Tax deducted/collected must be deposited within prescribed time (generally 7th of next month; April 30 for March TDS).
Quarterly TDS statements (Form 138/144/140) and TCS statements (Form 143) must be filed by specified due dates.
TDS certificates must be issued to deductees within prescribed time (Form 130/131/132).

flow.title: Compliance timeline for deductors
steps: Obtain TAN and PAN of deductee
Deposit tax by 7th of next month

topics.example: If a contractor fails to furnish PAN for a ₹50,000 contract, TDS is deducted at 20% instead of 1% or 2%.
remember: TDS deposit deadline: 7th of following month (30th April for March).
Non-furnishing of PAN rate: Higher of prescribed rate, rate in force, or 20% (5% for goods purchase).
mistakes: Forgetting that individual rent TDS (Sl. No. 2(i)) and property TDS (Sl. No. 3(i)) do NOT require TAN.

quiz.q: What is the higher TDS rate when deductee fails to furnish PAN, except for purchase of goods?
quiz.why: Under Section 397(2), failure to furnish PAN results in TDS at higher of prescribed rate, rate in force, or 20%.

quiz.q: What is the general due date for depositing TDS to the credit of Central Government for months other than March?
quiz.why: Rule 218 requires TDS deposited via IT challan to be paid on or before 7 days from the end of the month in which deduction is made.

topics.title: Consequences of Failure to Deduct or Collect Tax
explain: Failure to deduct/collect or pay tax makes the person a deemed 'assessee-in-default'.
Assessee-in-default status is waived if payee filed return u/s 263, included the income, paid tax due, and deductor submits accountant's certificate.
Interest for failure to deduct/collect tax: 1% per month or part of month from due date of deduction to actual date of deduction.
Interest for failure to pay deducted/collected tax: 1.5% per month or part of month from date of deduction to actual date of payment.

flow.title: Calculating interest on default
steps: Apply 1.5% p.m. for non-payment after deduction

topics.example: Tax deducted on 10th May but paid on 15th July attracts interest @1.5% p.m. for 3 months (May, June, July).
remember: Interest for non-deduction: 1% per month or part.
Interest for non-payment after deduction: 1.5% per month or part.
Part of a month is treated as a full month.
mistakes: Charging 1% interest for late payment of deducted tax instead of 1.5%.

quiz.q: What is the interest rate for failure to pay tax to the government AFTER deducting it at source?
quiz.why: Section 398(3)(a) levies 1.5% simple interest per month or part of a month for late payment after deduction.

quiz.q: How is a fraction of a month treated when calculating interest under Section 398?
quiz.why: Interest is calculated for every month or part of a month, meaning any fraction of a month is treated as a full month.

topics.title: Advance Tax Liability & Computation
explain: Advance tax is payable in the financial year on estimated current income if net tax liability is ₹10,000 or more.
Resident senior citizens (60+ years) having NO income under PGBP are exempt from paying advance tax.
Net advance tax payable = Estimated Tax Liability minus Tax Deducted/Collected at Source (TDS/TCS).
Assessees calculate current income via self-estimation without submitting estimates to Assessing Officer unless ordered.

flow.title: Advance tax calculation steps
steps: Calculate tax on total income at rates in force
Subtract estimated TDS and TCS credits
If net tax liability >= ₹10,000, advance tax is due

topics.example: A taxpayer with estimated tax of ₹50,000 and expected TDS of ₹42,000 has net tax payable of ₹8,000, so no advance tax is due (< ₹10,000).
remember: Advance tax threshold: Net tax payable >= ₹10,000.
Resident senior citizen with no PGBP income is exempt from advance tax.
mistakes: Including resident senior citizens with business income in the advance tax exemption.

quiz.q: What is the minimum net tax liability threshold that triggers advance tax payment obligation?
quiz.why: Section 404 states that obligation to pay advance tax arises when tax payable is ₹10,000 or more.

quiz.q: Which resident senior citizen is exempt from paying advance tax?
o: Senior citizen aged 60+ having no PGBP income
Senior citizen with total income below ₹10 lakhs
quiz.why: Section 403 exempts resident senior citizens (60+) who do not have any income under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession'.

topics.title: Advance Tax Instalments & Interest for Default or Deferment
explain: Advance tax instalments for corporates and non-corporates (4 instalments): 15% (15th June), 45% (15th Sept), 75% (15th Dec), 100% (15th March).
Presumptive taxation assessees u/s 58(2) pay 100% advance tax in a single instalment on or before 15th March.
Section 424 interest @ 1% p.m. applies if advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax.
Section 425 interest @ 3% (June/Sept/Dec shortfalls) and 1% (March shortfall) applies for deferment of instalments.
Shortfall due to unexpected capital gains, lottery winnings, or new business income does not attract Section 425 interest if tax is paid in remaining instalments.
topics.example: A company with ₹8 lakh tax liability must pay cumulative ₹6,00,000 (75%) by 15th December.
remember: Instalment due dates: June 15 (15%), Sept 15 (45%), Dec 15 (75%), Mar 15 (100%).
Section 424 interest: 1% p.m. if total advance tax < 90% of assessed tax.
mistakes: Calculating Section 425 deferment interest on the entire tax liability rather than the shortfall for that instalment.

quiz.q: By 15th September, what cumulative percentage of advance tax must be paid by a corporate assessee?
quiz.why: Section 408 requires cumulative advance tax paid by 15th September to be at least 45%.

quiz.q: Section 424 interest for default in payment of advance tax is triggered if advance tax paid is less than what percentage of assessed tax?
quiz.why: Section 424 levies interest if advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax.
